marketBrief.headline: Sunday, Nov. 15: Iran says tankers hit mines near Hormuz before futures reopen at 6 p.m. ET, and Bitcoin slips below $65,000, its lowest since July
marketBrief.summary: US stock and oil futures reopen at 6 p.m. ET, so this is a weekend preview, not a session recap. The IRGC Navy says two tankers struck mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz; no independent source has confirmed it. Brent settled at $95.84 and WTI at $88.56 on Friday, their second straight weekly decline (CNBC, citing Reuters). Bitcoin was quoted at $64,962 on Sunday (LiveMint).
bullets: Hormuz: the IRGC Navy says two tankers struck mines south of the strait (Anadolu; Tasnim). CBS News carried a three-tanker count and said the strikes could not be verified.

Oil: Brent $95.84 and WTI $88.56 at the Friday, Nov. 13 settle (CNBC, citing Reuters). Gulf-to-China supertanker freight eased to about 776 Worldscale from 841 but remains near records (Baltic Exchange data via PipeXchange).
Bitcoin: $64,962.10 in a Sunday LiveMint report, lowest since July. About $2 billion of 24-hour liquidations, mostly longs (Coinglass via LiveMint).
Rates: CME FedWatch put a Dec. 9 hike at 100%, with the 10-year at 5.143% on Friday (CNBC, Nov. 13). October PPI rose 0.3% m/m and 6.5% y/y (BLS).
Week ahead: Nvidia reports Nov. 17; retail sales and import prices land Nov. 17; FOMC minutes Nov. 18; Putin, Xi and Trump meet in Shenzhen Nov. 19 (Anadolu; Kremlin).
